issues.title: [1.21.1 NeoForge] NeoForge 21.1.262 breaks NetworkRegistryMixin (RETURN ordinal = 3): "Sided Packet Codec has not been unpacked", every player kicked on join
issues.body:
**Versions:** owo-lib 0.12.15.5-beta.1+1.21 (NeoForge), Accessories 1.1.0-beta.53+1.21.1, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge **21.1.262** (works on 21.1.259)

**What happens:** on NeoForge 21.1.262, every player is disconnected while joining a dedicated server:
```
Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload'
Failed encoding custom payload accessories:main: [owo] Sided Packet Codec has not been unpacked
```

**Cause:** `io.wispforest.owo.mixin.neoforge.NetworkRegistryMixin#owo$unpackSidedCodec` targets `NetworkRegistry.getCodec` with `@At(value = "RETURN", ordinal = 3)`.

NeoForge commit neoforged/NeoForge@0e98dad, shipped in 21.1.262 ("Enforce network setup payload directions and decoding limits"), added a new early `return null` inside the `BUILTIN_PAYLOADS` branch of that method. The RETURN ordinals in 21.1.262 are now:

| ordinal | return |
|---|---|
| 0 | `return null` (new: serverbound modded setup payloads) |
| 1 | `return BUILTIN_PAYLOADS.get(id)` |
| 2 | `return null` (no registration) |
| 3 | `return null` (flow mismatch) ← owo now modifies this one |
| 4 | `return registration.codec()` ← should be modified |
| 5 | `return null` (wrong phase) |

As a result, the `SidedPacketCodec` is never unpacked, and its `encode`/`decode` always throw. This breaks Accessories and every mod using owo networking on NeoForge 1.21.1. Hosts that auto-update the loader (for example Aternos) can't pin 21.1.259, so those servers are currently unjoinable.

**Suggested fix:** drop the ordinal so the unpacking applies to every return. The `instanceof` check already makes it a no-op for the other returns, and it works on both old and new NeoForge builds:

```java
@ModifyReturnValue(method = "getCodec", at = @At("RETURN"))
private static PacketCodec<? super PacketByteBuf, ? extends CustomPayload> owo$unpackSidedCodec(PacketCodec<? super PacketByteBuf, ? extends CustomPayload> original, @Local(argsOnly = true) NetworkSide flow) {
    if (original instanceof SidedPacketCodec<?> sidedPacketCodec) {
        original = (PacketCodec<? super PacketByteBuf, ? extends CustomPayload>) sidedPacketCodec.getCodec(flow);
    }
    return original;
}
```

(`original` can be `null` on the other returns. `instanceof` handles that.)

I also reported this to NeoForge: neoforged/NeoForge#3652. Forgified Fabric API has the same ordinal-3 pattern in its own `NetworkRegistryMixin`, so the NeoForge side may adjust as well. A release of owo-lib with this change would fix it regardless.

issues.title: [Bug] Missing Access Transformer file `META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg` in Pride Lib (`pride`)
issues.body:
### Summary
During game initialization, the mod loader reports that the Access Transformer file declared by the `pride` mod (`META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg`) is missing from the compiled JAR file. 

Because this configuration file is not found, the required access level modifications (widening field/method visibilities) are skipped during launch. This can lead to downstream runtime exceptions such as `NoSuchFieldError`, `NoSuchMethodError`, or `IllegalAccessError` when interacting with features or menus that depend on transformed members.

---

### Log Warning / Error
```text
Access transformer file META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg provided by mod pride does not exist!
```

---

### Impact & Potential Cause
1. **Unapplied Transformers:** Internal Minecraft/NeoForge fields or methods intended to be made public remain restricted.
2. **Runtime Failures:** Unhandled access restrictions will cause the game to crash or throw reflection/access errors upon accessing certain UI elements, items, or mod components.
3. **Build Configuration Issue:** The access transformer path is registered in the build script or mod metadata (`neoforge.mods.toml`), but the file was either omitted from the final JAR bundle or misplaced during compilation.

---

### Expected Behavior
- `META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg` should be present in the built JAR package if access transformation is required.
- Alternatively, if the Access Transformer is no longer needed, its declaration should be removed from the build configuration and mod metadata.

---

### Environment
- **Minecraft Version:** 1.21.1
- **Mod Loader:** NeoForge 21.1.259
- **Affected Mod:** Pride Lib (`pride`) / owo-lib
- **OS:** CachyOS(Linux) 

---

### Log File
- [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33361747/latest.log)

### Mod List
- [Sandbox (C) - Modlist.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33361749/Sandbox.C.-.Modlist.html)

issues.title: EdmOps throws a NullPointerException on null input instead of returning a DataResult error
issues.body:
### Versions

- Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248
- owo-lib 0.12.15.5-beta.1+1.21
- Accessories 1.1.0-beta.53+1.21.1
- Cold Sweat 2.4.3.1

### What happens

Putting armor that was insulated at Cold Sweat's sewing table into an Accessories cosmetic armor slot disconnects the player. The item stays in the slot, so the same packet is sent on every login and the player cannot rejoin until the save is edited.

reports of the same crash:

- wisp-forest/accessories#418
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#605
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#683
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#699


```
Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.DecoderException:
  Failed to decode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload'
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed decoding custom payload accessories:main:
  io.wispforest.endec.impl.StructField$StructFieldException:
  Exception occurred when decoding a given StructField: [Field: dirtyCosmeticStacks]
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException:
  Cannot invoke "io.wispforest.endec.format.edm.EdmElement.value()" because "input" is null
    at io.wispforest.owo.serialization.format.edm.EdmOps.getStringValue(EdmOps.java:157)
    at com.mojang.serialization.Codec$16.read / PrimitiveCodec.decode
    at com.momosoftworks.coldsweat.data.codec.impl.ConfigData.decodeFromMap(ConfigData.java:99)
    at com.momosoftworks.coldsweat.data.codec.impl.ConfigData$1.decode(ConfigData.java:69)
    at io.wispforest.owo.serialization.CodecUtils.decodeWithCodecFromDeserializer(CodecUtils.java:98)
```

### Cause

`EdmOps.getStringValue` calls `input.value()` without checking `input`. The same goes for `getNumberValue`, `getBooleanValue`, `getByteBuffer`, `getStream` and `getMapValues` (the last two compare against `empty()` first and then call `input.value()`).

`NbtOps` and `JsonOps` use an `instanceof` check, so a null input gives them a `DataResult.error`. Some codecs depend on that. Cold Sweat reads optional keys like this:

```java
codec.decode(ops, input.get(key)).result().map(Pair::getFirst).orElse(defaultValue)
```

`MapLike.get` returns null for a missing key, the decode fails, and the default is used. With `EdmOps` the decode throws instead. In this case the missing keys are `registry_name` and `registry_key` inside the `cold_sweat:armor_insulation` component, which are only written when the insulator comes from a registry.

Passing null to a codec is arguably sloppy on Cold Sweat's side, but it works with the vanilla ops, so any mod that does the same will break whenever its data goes through `CodecUtils.toEndec`.

### Suggested fix

Return the existing error result when `input` is null in the read methods of `EdmOps`, for example:

```java
public DataResult<String> getStringValue(EdmElement<?> input) {
    if (input != null && input.value() instanceof String value) return DataResult.success(value);
    return DataResult.error(() -> "Not a string: " + input);
}
```

`mergeToList`, `mergeToMap`, `remove` and `convertTo` dereference their input the same way. I have not seen them hit.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Accessories, owo-lib and Cold Sweat.
2. Add any insulator to an armor piece at the Sewing Table.
3. Open the Accessories screen, show the cosmetic slots, and put the armor into the matching cosmetic armor slot.

### Workaround

I made a small mixin mod that adds the null check to the six read methods: https://github.com/neonishere/owo-null-fix

issues.title: NullPointerException in ConfigureHotReloadScreen after retargeting owo:configure_hot_reload via /owo-ui-set-reload-path
issues.body:
> Note: This description was written by me, grammar-overhauled by Claude for the Pull Request, and now adapted for this Issue.

Setting a reload path for owo's own `owo:configure_hot_reload` screen (instead of a mod's own screen) via `/owo-ui-set-reload-path owo:configure_hot_reload` bricks the command permanently - every subsequent `/owo-ui-set-reload-path` invocation crashes with a `NullPointerException` at `ConfigureHotReloadScreen.java:39`, since the screen tries to build itself from the (invalid) reload target instead of its own model. 1. Run `/owo-ui-set-reload-path owo:configure_hot_reload`

issues.title: Memory usage impact of `DerivedComponentMap`
issues.body:
While analyzing memory usage in All The Mods 10 for FerriteCore (total heap: 4.5 GB), I noticed that owolibs `DerivedComponentMap` feature increases memory usage by about 350 MB. I think the root cause is that the logic is applied to all stacks (about 2.75M instances in memory), rather than just those for items that implement a nontrivial `deriveStackComponents` (i.e. a very small fraction).

The additional memory usage has two separate causes:
- Calling `PatchedDataComponentMap::applyPatch`/`ComponentMapImpl::setChanges` on a newly initialized component map will call `ensureMapOwnership`, even if the argument is an empty map as it is [here](https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/a617567c207d2666db27564a7fd8f4290f129090/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ext/DerivedComponentMap.java#L33-L36). This causes the singleton returned by `Reference2ObjectMaps.emptyMap` to be replaced with a new `Reference2ObjectArrayMap`, which uses 72 extra bytes per stack. Since nearly all stacks in memory have empty patches, this means an extra memory usage of `72 * 2.75M = 198 MB`. I implemented a more general fix for memory usage from these empty maps in the latest release for FerriteCore, but I think it would still be good if this was fixed on your end as well.
- Even when this is resolved, the feature results in noticeably increased memory usage. This usage is simply from the presence of two new object for each `ItemStack` instance, one `DerivedComponentMap` (24 bytes shallow) and the `PatchedDataComponentMap`/`ComponentMapImpl` stored in it (32 bytes shallow). This works out to `56 * 2.75M = 154 MB` of additional memory usage.

issues.title: Proxy Service Flags for Custom Modpack
issues.body:
Hello. 

First I understand that this isn't really an issue but more a question on my part as to how to go about implementing a specific flag on a packwiz backed Prism/MultiMC instance. 

For context, we use a Gate Reverse Proxy service for our Minecraft Servers. Unfortunately, owo's handshake doesn't work with Gate. There is a workaround to disable the handshake, as given here: [System Properties](https://docs.wispforest.io/owo/system-properties#dowo-handshake-disable-true-false).

That said, I have been unable to determine how to implement this on a Prism/MultiMC setup. I know Prism instances are capable of this as we are able to use official modpacks like RLCraft and Cobblemon without issue on our Gate Proxy, but I cannot find where the property is set. issues.title: OwoUIDrawContext#intersectsScissor(PositionRectangle) not respecting MatrixStack transformation

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: this issue breaks or otherwise adversely affects functionality

labels.name: priority: normal
labels.description: this issue does not break any critical functionality - it must be adressed, but not immediately

labels.name: status: confirmed
labels.description: this issue is reproducible or otherwise confirmed to exist

issues.body:
Minecraft's `DrawContext#enableScissor(int, int, int, int)` transformes the Scissor according to the MatrixStack:
(Snipper)
```java
public void enableScissor(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2) {
  ScreenRect screenRect = (new ScreenRect(x1, y1, x2 - x1, y2 - y1)).transform(this.matrices);
  this.scissorStack.push(screenRect);
}
```

However, owo's intersectsScissor does not respect that transformation:

https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/94e0c3779737e43b5bbcb35629db6500646c45f2/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/core/OwoUIDrawContext.java#L64-L75

This is fine as long as the translation is 0,0.
When rendering a toast for example, then it is not possible to use `OwoUIAdapter`, because it scissors the entire screen (which isn't an issue):
https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/94e0c3779737e43b5bbcb35629db6500646c45f2/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/core/OwoUIAdapter.java#L180-L182
But then `BaseParentComponent` checks for the scissor intersection before drawing:
https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/94e0c3779737e43b5bbcb35629db6500646c45f2/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/base/BaseParentComponent.java#L349
The scissor intersection returns false, even though it should return true. And the toast won't render.

issues.title: The command-line installer is preventing game from start or crash in a way barely noticeable
issues.body:
Hi. Just some experience today, not sure if it's relevant here.

Today I was trying to add a few mods to my game instance using Modrinth launcher. After hitting the install button I thought the dependency was handled automatically, which isn't true actually. The mod I installed is Accessories which depends on **owo-lib**, which was not downloaded together. From my experience this normally causes a popup during launch that tells you which mods are required but not present. However, nothing happened, and the game window never showed up. The game starting process hung for about 20 minutes and the log output in Modrinth App just stopped at the line "loading N mods: *all the mods*", with no warnings, no extra information about the hang. I had to terminate the bootup and give another try, but in vain. The game still hung without any reason.

I checked the logs and unsurprisingly they holds the content identical to the console output I saw in Modrinth. At the moment I decided to reinstall the game, I peeked the `launcher_log.txt` which might be generated by the app and saw some extra lines after the "loading mods" line:
```
// ... all the mods
	   |-- com_twelvemonkeys_imageio_imageio-metadata 3.12.0
	   |-- com_twelvemonkeys_imageio_imageio-webp 3.12.0
	   |-- org_quiltmc_parsers_gson 0.2.1
	   \-- org_quiltmc_parsers_json 0.2.1
oωo-lib is required to run the following mods:
- Accessories (explicit dependency)

oωo-lib is a library used by most mods under the
Wisp Forest domain to ease development. This is
simply a convenient installer, as oωo is missing from your
installation. Should you not trust it, feel free to head to the
repository and download oωo yourself.

Download and install (Y/n):

# Process exited with status: signal: 9 (SIGKILL)

```

SIGKILL is my terminating act. Suddenly I know what's happening, why it would hang and why it never crashed. I think this behaviour is somewhat unreasonable in this client-side scenario as you barely have the chance or thought to make your confirmation in the console when you're just playing on your own laptop. It would be more ideal to just crash.

Also, I'm so confused about the missing of these extra confirmation lines in the console output which you can see directly in the App, and `latest.log` which is my first option when checking something. Any explanation on this is appreciated!

I'm not sure if this behaviour is relevant to this repository, but this is the first place I come up with to give the information. Sorry if I bothered anyone.

issues.title: owo-lib Config Screen: Integer Slider with @RangeConstraint(min=1) Visually Defaults to 0 on Initial

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: this issue breaks or otherwise adversely affects functionality

issues.body:
# I'm seeing a visual issue with an integer slider in my mod's config (MC 1.21.1, owo-lib 0.12.15.4+1.21).

## **Problem:**
An `int` option, `maxGroupSize`, is defined in my [`ModConfigModel.java`](https://github.com/DawsonBodenhamer/Adorable-Hamster-Pets-1.21/blob/320fccfddf1100c4c7f41c2e75f4d60785b67a28/src/main/java/net/dawson/adorablehamsterpets/config/ModConfigModel.java#L45) with `@RangeConstraint(min = 1, max = 10)` and a default of `1`. The generated `ModConfig.java` and the `adorablehamsterpets.json5` file correctly reflect this default or user-set values. Game logic uses the correct value fine.

## The UI issue:
1.  **Initial Display:** On first opening the config screen, the `maxGroupSize` slider *shows* **0**.
2.  **Click Behavior:** Clicking the slider (without dragging) makes it jump to **1**.
3.  **Reset Button:** Works correctly, sets to **1**.
4.  **Re-opening Screen:** If changed, then "Done" is clicked, re-opening the config screen shows the slider back at **0** visually, though the `.json5` file and game logic use the correct saved value.

### It seems the UI slider might not apply the min constraint for its initial visual render or doesn't immediately display the loaded/default value correctly.

## [**Video of the issue:**](https://youtu.be/SUoMNS7MoBs)

## **@Blodhgarm** on Discord said: 

> "Can you try setting the decimal places to 0 in the attribute? The attribute has control over how much precision there is and I wonder if its just a visual glitch with rounding and I wound if setting the value from 2 to 0 it will show the correct value."

So I followed his instruction like this, 
```
@Comment("Maximum hamsters per spawn group. Because sometimes one just isn't cute enough.")
        @RangeConstraint(min = 1, max = 10, decimalPlaces = 0)
        public int maxGroupSize = 1;
```
But it did not fix the issue.

Any ideas what might cause this visual-only discrepancy or if there's a known workaround?

Thanks!

labels.name: platform: neo
labels.description: this issue is about the neoforge version of owo-lib

issues.body:
I am running a custom modpack. It only seems to crash on one PC, but runs on 5 other PCs just fine. I think it's related to owo-lib based on the crash logs, but I am not sure. The crash happens on launch. I've tried changing RAM settings, Using Java 21, and removing mods such as Lighty, Immersive UI, Iris, and Seamless Loading Screen.

https://mclo.gs/SpQ0KvR#L478

issues.title: KSP annotation processor
issues.body:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32c060b4-7794-4c47-b32b-443340757aa7)
## Why
Currently kotlin requires Kapt to be able to use a java annotation processor, otherwise kotlin source code is invisible.
## How
Implement a KSP annotation processor to use for creating configurations

## Links
https://kotlinlang.org/docs/kapt.html
https://kotlinlang.org/docs/ksp-overview.html
https://kotlinlang.org/docs/ksp-reference.html
https://github.com/square/kotlinpoet

issues.title: Unable to Block /owo-config Command with FTB Ranks & Player Roles - LootBalls / OwoLib
issues.body:
Hello,

I have encountered an issue with OwoLib. The command /owo-config allows all players, including those in the default group (everyone), to modify the mod's configuration, creating a potential security risk for public servers.

I have attempted to block this command using:
✔ FTB Ranks (ftb-ranks-fabric-2001.1.3.jar)
✔ Player Roles (player-roles-1.6.6.jar)

➡ Issue: Despite these restrictions, players can still execute /owo-config and modify the mod settings.

📌 Steps to Reproduce the Bug:
- Install LootBalls and OwoLib on a Fabric server.
- Add a non-op player to the default group (everyone).
- Attempt to block /owo-config using FTB Ranks or Player Roles (roles.json).
- Test if the player can still run /owo-config and modify settings.

📌 Expected Behavior:
- The /owo-config command should not be accessible to non-admin players.
- FTB Ranks and Player Roles should properly block the command and prevent unauthorized use.

📌 Environment Details:
- LootBalls Version: 1.1.4
- OwoLib Version: 0.11.2+1.20
- FTB Ranks Version: 2001.1.3
- Player Roles Version: 1.6.6

📌 Additional Information:
- Other server commands are correctly blocked by FTB Ranks and Player Roles, indicating that this issue is specific to LootBalls / OwoLib.
- There is no configuration option in the mod files to disable this command manually.
🔹 Please investigate this issue and provide a fix to ensure /owo-config is properly restricted.

issues.title: [Enhancement] Option to disable wisdom logging
issues.body:
Some wisdom statements can be seen as crass or inappropriate. 

Additionally, for troubleshooting it does effectively nothing if you dont know where the line is coming from. Ideally it should either be defaulted to only show in debug mode or when a config value is enabled. at minimum, it would be best to have a config option to disable it so that logs arent clogged with random, useless things.

issues.title: Bug Report: oωo Mod Network Packet Registration Issue

labels.name: platform: neo
labels.description: this issue is about the neoforge version of owo-lib

issues.body:
[crash-2025-01-18_12.35.58-fml.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18464267/crash-2025-01-18_12.35.58-fml.txt)

## Environment
- Minecraft Version: 1.21.1
- Forge Type: NeoForge
- NeoForge Version: 21.1.95
- oωo Mod Version: 0.12.15-beta.12+1.21
- Operating System: Windows 11 (amd64) version 10.0
- Java Version: 21.0.5 (Azul Systems, Inc.)
- Available Memory: 4096 MiB

## Issue Description
Intermittent crash during mod loading related to network packet registration. The crash does not occur consistently but appears randomly during game startup.

## Error Message
```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot register handler as no payload type has been registered with name "owo:local_packet" for CLIENTBOUND PLAY
```

## Stack Trace
The error originates in the Fabric Networking API bridge:
```
at TRANSFORMER/fabric_networking_api_v1@4.2.2+a92978fd19/org.sinytra.fabric.networking_api.NeoCommonNetworking.assertPayloadType(NeoCommonNetworking.java:20)
at TRANSFORMER/fabric_networking_api_v1@4.2.2+a92978fd19/org.sinytra.fabric.networking_api.client.NeoClientPlayNetworking.registerGlobalReceiver(NeoClientPlayNetworking.java:31)
at TRANSFORMER/fabric_networking_api_v1@4.2.2+a92978fd19/net.fabricmc.fabric.api.client.networking.v1.ClientPlayNetworking.registerGlobalReceiver(ClientPlayNetworking.java:71)
at TRANSFORMER/owo@0.12.15-beta.12+1.21/io.wispforest.owo.client.screens.ScreenInternals$Client.init(ScreenInternals.java:79)
at TRANSFORMER/owo@0.12.15-beta.12+1.21/io.wispforest.owo.client.OwoClient.<init>(OwoClient.java:79)
```

## Technical Details
The crash appears to be related to the initialization of network packets in the client-side component of the mod. Specifically:
1. The error occurs during the registration of a global receiver for "owo:local_packet"
2. The crash happens in the ScreenInternals$Client initialization
3. The issue involves the Fabric Networking API bridge component

## Reproduction
- The issue is inconsistent and does not occur on every launch
- No specific steps have been identified to reliably reproduce the issue
- The crash occurs during the mod loading phase before reaching the main menu

## Additional Context
The mod is running alongside 150+ other mods (full list in the crash report). Given the intermittent nature of the crash and the involvement of network packet registration, this could potentially be a race condition or timing issue during mod initialization.

## Fabric API Components Present
- Fabric API Base: 0.4.42+d1308dedd1
- Fabric Networking API v1: 4.2.2+a92978fd19
- Fabric Screen API v1: 2.0.24+79a4c2b0d1

## System Specifications
- CPU: 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz
- RAM: 16GB (2x8GB DDR4 @ 3.20GHz)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (6GB VRAM)

I've currently on owo-lib on a project because my project is using Accessories which has the lib embedded so it's in my project too while I'm working with Accessories.

My only request is please make this an opt-in feature within the lib. issues.body:

When using the @PredicateConstraint in my config model, the value inside the input box appears green, even though the value does not satisfy the @PredicateConstraint. This gives the impression that the input is valid, which can be misleading for users. The only sign that the config value didn't get saved is a log message, that is probably overlooked by most users.

![grafik](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2c27fb2-c567-4775-b11c-994b421b0cae)

`[Render thread/WARN] (owo) Option Key{path=[maxMediaSize]} in config 'mod' could not be updated, as the given value '-123' does not match its constraint: Predicate method maxMediaSizePredicate`
_The only sign that the config didn't get saved. Probably overlooked by most users_

**Expected Behavior:**
The input box should visually indicate when a @PredicateConstraint is not satisfied by turning the text red, similar to how other invalid inputs are indicated.

(I have only tested this with int values)

My Code:
```
@PredicateConstraint("maxMediaSizePredicate")
public int maxMediaSize = 30;
public static boolean maxMediaSizePredicate(int maxMediaSize) {
        return maxMediaSize > 0;
}

issues.title: Shaders Not Rendering
jvm crash upon inventory exit when cursors aren't installed on system
issues.body:
two parts to this!
1. when any requested cursor in CursorAdapter isn't available on your operating system, glfw returns a null pointer. passing the null pointer to glfwDestroyCursor trips LWJGL's Checks, throwing a nullpointerexception.
2. the npe then causes the current screen to be destructed, re-calling destruct on CursorAdapter, calling glfwDestroyCursor on already-freed cursors, resulting in a JVM segfault

easy fix would be filtering for nulls (well, in this case, 0s) before calling glfwDestroyCursor (and also setting the destructed variable before destroying the cursors instead of after)

`BaseComponent.drawChildren()` [gets the current focus handler](https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/68b0aa6c590264ab5013340fe9af6e7d0421709d/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/base/BaseParentComponent.java#L346) and [checks if the highlight should be drawn](https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/68b0aa6c590264ab5013340fe9af6e7d0421709d/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/base/BaseParentComponent.java#L355). However, `ParentComponent.focusHandler()` allows nullable return value, so calling `focusHandler.lastFocusSource()` can cause a `NullPointerException`.

So uh, insert a `if (focusHandler != null && ...)`

issues.title: `ConfigWrapper` shouldn't clinit `Screen`
issues.body:
Currently, `ConfigWrapper` [clinits `ConfigScreen`](https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/1.21/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/config/ConfigWrapper.java#L91-L94), which clinits Screen because it's its superclass.
`Screen` has a static `RotatingCubeMapRenderer ROTATING_PANORAMA_RENDERER` field which is initted in `<clinit>` and which captures the current `MinecraftClient`, which if it's early enough in the game will be null. This will cause a NPE later in the runtime.

WorldEdit for 1.21 (7.3.4) Requires `com.google.guava:guava:{strictly 32.1.3-jre}` while owo-lib requires `com.google.guava:guava:33.0.0-jre`, the former matches what minecraft itself has while the latter does not.

Checking 1.21's .json file:
`            "name": "com.google.guava:guava:32.1.2-jre"`

Yes somehow both are mismatches (even though worldedit claims it matches), but owo-lib is very much mismatched, which makes any compilation using both to fail.

Also of note: `fastutil` is also ahead: `it.unimi.dsi:fastutil:8.5.12` in Minecraft & WorldEdit, `it.unimi.dsi:fastutil:8.5.13` in owo-lib

issues.title: [Suggestion] [owo-ui] Add scrollable text in case it doesn't fit in
issues.body:
## Description

It would be good for owo-lib to support ClickableWidget.drawScrollableText. This is useful in case the component has a certain width and exceeds it. This can happen in situations like parameters (for example, if it's an item and they use Waxed Exposed Cut Copper Stairs, clearly you're not going to change the size just for this specific case) or translations

### ButtonComponent
currently, if a horizontal sizing is not specified, the content sizing adjusts to the text. If a horizontal sizing is set and it exceeds it, the text overflows the button. In contrast, vanilla in recent versions uses ClickableWidget.drawScrollableText, you can see it on some buttons if you change the language (for example, Spanish in the accessibility screen)

### LabelComponent
currently, if a horizontal sizing is not specified, the content sizing adjusts to the label. If a horizontal sizing is set, and in case it exceeds it, it breaks into multiple lines. It would be nice to have an option that requires a horizontal sizing and uses ClickableWidget.drawScrollableText

### OwoUIDrawContext
perhaps it would be good to add OwoUIDrawContext.drawScrollableText? In case someone needs to use it and thus avoids having to use an access widener

issues.body:
## Description
When using a FlowLayout with a gap, if one of the components within it uses sizing with the 'extend' method, it will detect the gap as empty, causing the component to become too large. This doesn't happen if margins are used instead of a gap.

## Code
```xml
<!-- expand + gap, bug -->
<flow-layout direction="horizontal">
    <children>
        <flow-layout direction="vertical">
            <children>
                <!-- ... -->
            </children>

            <sizing>
                <vertical method="fixed">20</vertical>
                <horizontal method="fixed">20</horizontal>
            </sizing>

            <surface>
                <panel/>
            </surface>
        </flow-layout>

        <flow-layout direction="vertical">
            <children>
                <!-- ... -->
            </children>

            <sizing>
                <vertical method="fixed">20</vertical>
                <horizontal method="expand">100</horizontal>
            </sizing>

            <surface>
                <panel/>
            </surface>
        </flow-layout>
    </children>

    <gap>10</gap>
</flow-layout>

<!-- margins -->
<flow-layout direction="horizontal">
    <children>
        <flow-layout direction="vertical">
            <children>
                <!-- ... -->
            </children>

            <sizing>
                <vertical method="fixed">20</vertical>
                <horizontal method="fixed">20</horizontal>
            </sizing>

            <surface>
                <panel/>
            </surface>

            <margins>
                <right>10</right>
            </margins>
        </flow-layout>

        <flow-layout direction="vertical">
            <children>
                <!-- ... -->
            </children>

            <sizing>
                <vertical method="fixed">20</vertical>
                <horizontal method="expand">100</horizontal>
            </sizing>

            <surface>
                <panel/>
            </surface>
        </flow-layout>
    </children>
</flow-layout>
```

## Versions

owo_version=0.12.5+1.20.3
minecraft_version=1.20.4
fabric_version=0.96.4+1.20.4

issues.body:
As seen in https://github.com/Noaaan/MythicMetals/issues/178

JEI seems to populate its recipe viewer by looking at items in creative groups. This causes some weirdness with owo-lib and its tabbed itemgroups, as only the items from the current selected tab is loaded when JEI reloads. I have reproduced this in the following way:
- Join a world where you have a tabbed owo-itemgroup with custom items
- Check JEI, as its missing some items
- Select another tab
- Rejoin the world to reload JEI, the items are now replaced 

I am not familiar with JEI code, so unsure what the fix to this is. From previous internal discussions JEI could in theory grab the items from elsewhere, even within itemgroups, which should always hold all the items of the group. We could also in theory make explicit compat for supplying the items somehow, although the scope of that is unknown to me.

labels.name: type: enhancement

labels.name: priority: low

labels.description: this issue is not easily reproducible or fixable, the cause is being investigated

issues.body:
# Why and Design

Considering that owo-lib has long had the amazing container and reflection design of the \*\*\*RegistryContainer, and provides an easy-to-use registration feature based on it, could we not provide an even easier DataGeneration feature based on this design?

In this case, I tried using annotations to mark up the field and use reflection on it early on, and I think this is a good fit for the way owo-lib uses reflection: use the information about the field to process it accordingly, and use annotations to attach additional information to the field.

## Examples

These are some of my early designs and uses.

### Basic Infomation Attatch

I considered use annotations to attach infomation to field, this is the most common generic practice.

But there is a downside to this approach, which is that if there is too much information to be attached to the annotations, they can become very lengthy.

Here is an example:

```java
@AssignedName("test")                       // Already in owo-lib.
@Recipe("test_recipe")                      // Maybe we can scanning recipe object and storage it in a hashmap?
@Tag("issues:test", type = TagType.Block)   // Or also scan and storage tag information in a hasmap?
@Model(type = ModelType.NoModel)            // Provide some pre-built models. Here the choice is not to generate.
public static final Block TEST_BLOCK;
```

For example the text of
```xml
<text-box>
    <max-length>300</max-length>
    <text>This is an example text longer than 32 chars, which is the default limit</text>
</text-box>
```
will get trimmed to `This is an example text longer t`

the text is set before the maximum length and the text setter trims the text if it is to long.

issues.title: Buggy Interaction with Gearifiers/Gear Core
issues.body:
After a few days of wading through various modpacks with the help of several people in this issue: fzzyhmstrs/gearifiers#2 , it seems like we've narrowed down to **owo-lib** as a source of conflict with attribute modifiers.

The gist of the problem can be seen in various videos posted in that issue thread; the TL;DW is that attribute modifiers added by the affixes from Gearifers/Gear Core are applied when gear is equipped, but are not (always) un-applied when the gear is removed. This only happens with owo installed. Without it, affixes come on and off equally, as expected. 

I've tested this just with owo, fabric api, and Gearifiers + needed deps for that. Latest versions for all mods (1.19.2)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72876796/222874406-2a3f9dab-fab3-493e-9959-690f231e70bd.png)


This leads to attributes stacking up improperly until the player relogs. For example, you can see below that I am wearing zero armor, however, I still have 4 armor. This is after equipping and unequipping the leather pants right below the boot slot several times. They are affixed with my Legendary modifier (below):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72876796/222872478-142f540a-99b5-4554-a77a-a052e001df50.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72876796/222872508-712a777d-5f51-49cd-a7b4-276b5370868a.png)

This doesn't seem to happen when my affixes have any old type of attribute incorporated.. So far movement speed seems to be the culprit. If a piece of gear has an affix with speed included, the issue happens. There may be others, but I haven't tested through all my affixes yet.

Make Components.list utility function use `Collection` instead of `List`
issues.body:
Hey hi there! Quick tiny thing - The `list()` function could be a little easier to work with if it only required a `Collection` rather than a `List`. The implementation only iterates through them, so it shouldn't mind it being any kind of collection

https://github.com/wisp-forest/owo-lib/blob/dd38739c82070e0cea5c4c037f1c53d41cb4623c/src/main/java/io/wispforest/owo/ui/component/Components.java#L134-L136

Stuff like `Map.values()` returns collections but not lists, and It'd save a bit of extra constructing.

issues.title: Can't join LAN world on a client without this mod

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: this issue breaks or otherwise adversely affects functionality

labels.name: status: scheduled
labels.description: the resolution of this issue is scheduled for the next release

issues.body:
## Description
Creating a LAN world when owolib is installed prevents players without the library from joining, even though owolib (in my case) was only used for a client-only mod.
The mod I first noticed the issue with was [PocketWatch](https://modrinth.com/mod/pocketwatch), however I figured this was likely not an issue with PocketWatch, but rather with the library.
And indeed, even with owolib installed in isolation, it prevents players without it from joining.

## Reproduction steps
1. Install `owo-lib-0.8.5+1.19` and `quilted-fabric-api-4.0.0-beta.19+0.64.0-1.19.2` on a Quilt Loader 0.17.6 client
2. Create a world and share it to LAN with this _owolib client_
3. Launch another client, either vanilla or another modded on **without owolib**, and try to join the LAN world
:x: -> You will receive an error message

The following errors will be produced respectively:
- Trying to join with another quilt client with no owo-lib results in:
  ```
   Missing entries for registry "minecraft:sound_event":
   -  owo:ui.owo.interaction
   ``` 
- Trying to join with a vanilla client results in: **Unsupported (vanilla?) client.*

Hope I could provide all necessary information to help you debug the issue.

## Solution
Detect if a LAN world is running and not a normal server, and don't enable owolibs server features, but run it as if it was client only on the hosting client.

issues.body:
This system variable can be useful when trying to make mods using owo-lib working with mods like [PolyMC](https://github.com/TheEpicBlock/PolyMc).
I get that it's not an intended use of the lib or in the library's focus at all but to someone this can be helpful.
Maybe it can be listed as a unsupported use of the library, the mods using this library and it should be used at your own risk?

issues.title: Handshake Failure
issues.body:
I attempted to use this numerous times running on Fabric in a docker container. Each time I get handshake failure incompatible client. As soon as the plugin is removed everything works fine. 

Steps to reproduce issue -
Deploy docker of itzg/minecraft-server:latest
Type = FABRIC
launcher = 0.10.2
Loader = 0.14.4

have this mod install and start server
once server is started you will not be able to connect due to handshake failure.

issues.body:
As far as I can tell, the default behaviour when there is only one registered sub-tab in the OwoItemGroup is to actually display no sub-tabs and treat the content as if it is part of the main creative tab.

I'd like to be able to force that sub-tab to render, regardless of the fact that there is only a single tab. Is this possible? I tried to search through the javadoc, maybe I missed something?
